svg.title: Analysis decision flow
svg.desc: A shared flow-accounting gate records eligible, excluded, failed and scored units with reasons. The diagram then divides into a quantitative branch and a qualitative branch. The quantitative branch requires denominators and distributions, checks dependence and units, permits exact paired binary or conditional Wilcoxon-style analysis only when assumptions and sample support them, reports effect sizes and uncertainty, and preserves multiplicity, strata, sensitivity, failures, negative, null and regressive outcomes. The qualitative branch admits only the predefined nine-family error taxonomy and consented reviewer feedback, creates a case-by-code framework matrix, versions coding and disagreement records, and retains patterns and negative cases. Both branches meet at integrated limitations. A final stop states that the exact statistical method and sample size remain TO FREEZE after D1 variance and annotation evidence plus supervisor and statistical review. The figure is conceptual and contains no inferential result.
svg.text: Analysis decision flow
Dependence-aware quantitative analysis and auditable qualitative interpretation.
CONCEPTUAL / NO RESULTS
FLOW ACCOUNTING BEFORE ANALYSIS
Eligible | excluded | failed | scored units - each with denominator and reason.
Publish descriptive distributions before any inferential choice.
QUANTITATIVE BRANCH
QUALITATIVE BRANCH
Q1 | DENOMINATORS + DESCRIPTIVES
Per-condition denominators, distributions and missingness.
No test precedes flow accounting.
Q2 | DEPENDENCE / UNIT CHECK
Pair the same company-period or claim.
Repeated fields and claims are not independent.
Aggregate by report/company or use cluster-aware CI.
Q3 | METHOD FAMILY - ONLY IF SUPPORTED
Binary paired outcomes: an exact paired method may fit.
Non-normal paired time/edit outcomes: Wilcoxon-style
analysis only if assumptions and sample support it.
The exact method is not selected here.
Q4 | EFFECT + UNCERTAINTY
Report effect size and interval, not p-values alone.
Name unit, estimator, assumptions and failures.
Q5 | MULTIPLICITY, STRATA + SENSITIVITY
Predeclare multiplicity handling or label exploratory.
Stratify only where the sample supports interpretation.
Repeat with failures and justified exclusions included.
Preserve negative, null and unexpected regressions.
K1 | AUTHORISED INPUTS ONLY
Pre-defined error taxonomy + consented reviewer feedback.
No feedback without authority and consent.
K2 | PRE-DEFINED CODE FAMILIES
ID
EXT
NORM
TIME
PROV
VER
REP
SEC
HITL
K3 | CASE-BY-CODE FRAMEWORK MATRIX
Rows = cases; columns = code families and additions.
Retain exact report, claim, event and feedback locator.
K4 | VERSIONED CODING + DISAGREEMENT
Record coder, codebook/version, reason and resolution.
No silent overwrite; agreement is not source truth.
K5 | PATTERNS, NEGATIVE CASES + LIMITS
Compare patterns within and across cases.
Retain contradictions, minority patterns and exceptions.
Report consent, coverage and researcher influence.
Do not turn purposive feedback counts into population
frequencies or generalised prevalence.
INTEGRATED INTERPRETATION
Effect and uncertainty + patterns and negative cases -> explicit limitations.
Keep executed evidence, evidence class and unresolved holds visible.
STOP / TO FREEZE
Exact statistical method and sample size are not selected now
Wait for D1 variance/annotation evidence + supervisor/statistical review.
No inferential result is asserted.
Source: Demsar (2006, PDF pp. 5-9); DiCiccio & Efron (1996, pp. 1-4); Gale et al. (2013, pp. 3-7);
Artstein & Poesio (2008, pp. 2-8, 26-28); Kapoor & Narayanan (2023, pp. 1-7); Pineau et al. (2021, pp. 1-5);
NIST (2023, pp. 33-35) and the current draft evaluation protocol. Exact local files/hashes: TXT + provenance.
Faye Niu | METH-F3 | author synthesis; conceptual and non-empirical; preserve negative, null and regressive outcomes.
